analysis:
Reviewed head-side excerpts of ClusterService.swift (lines 473-1339): relay tick, peer port query, syncMembers, receive/command handlers, solo readiness, status, update/approval checks, and supervision. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the later hunks (around 1301, 1428, and 1448-1463) and the use of the new `environment` parameter in `partEnvironment` were not visible. I could not verify how the environment override is applied when a part starts. That integration question needs the full patch.

Observed controls that look intact:
- `command()` .serve/.stop checks the claim term and `followsPeer(pairing)`.
- The link exchange is pairing-authenticated with a pinned peer. `syncMembers` checks `pairing.peerPin == leadership.peerPin`.
- `soloAnswers` sends the local API token only to our own verified solo child. Another program on the port is probed without the token (lines 763-770).
- The relay is only opened when the record shows scope.bind == "0.0.0.0" and the saved role is not leader (lines 483-484). It forwards to the paired peer's rank 0 port, which comes from the status reply of the authenticated link.
- `relayTick` writes a discovery file containing the cluster token with host 0.0.0.0. That is pre-existing behavior and is guarded by the live-info pid check.
- `stopLeftover` signals only a process whose pid and start time match the recorded part, so a recycled pid is not signalled.
- `receive()` applies the leader's setup through `ClusterConsoleObserver.approve` with the expected SHA, so the leader's word adds no trust.

The only visible changes in this range are at lines 1131-1133, where the approval set-aside logic is reworked. It still only sets `approvalSetAside` when the step produces one and the result changed, and clears it on `.save`. No security regression is evident in the visible portions.

Threat IDs touched indirectly: TB-003 and A-008 (local token handling). Neither is changed.
